tier_reason: Downgraded C to D: the python-blosc README numbers come from the v1.5.x bench/compress_ptr.py, whose memcpy baseline writes into freshly np.empty-allocated memory (page faults on 800 MB) while compress writes only cbytes into a preallocated bytes object, and the pasted thread counts cannot come from the unmodified script (AssemblyScript precedent: baseline crippled by the harness).

corrections.caveats: python-blosc README numbers (1.5.1.dev0) compare one single-threaded memmove against 24-thread Blosc in single-shot GiB/s timings on randint(0,1001) int64 'random' data, so every input compresses well; no compiler flags. The v1.5.x bench/compress_ptr.py allocates the memmove and decompress destinations with np.empty right before timing, so the 0.276 s memcpy baseline includes page faults on 800 MB of fresh memory while compress only writes cbytes into an oversized bytes object (blosc_extension.c v1.5.0 lines 200 and 245; the np.full prefault arrived in v1.9.0), inflating the 6.6x compress figure. The script prints blosc.ncores with a default of min(ncores,4), yet the pasted output shows 'Detected cores: 56', 'default: 4' and '24 threads', so it was edited or came from a modified script. Open crash issues #385 (invalid write near 2 GB) and #402 (GCC 15 -ftree-vectorize segfault, no reply). Maintenance mode, last release v1.21.6 (2024-06-24); c-blosc2 is the active successor.
